The first public release of **datum**, a command-line tool that hides any file inside the pixel values of an image or a video and gets it back byte for byte.

Unlike tools that append data to the end of a file, `datum` writes the payload into the pixels themselves. The output is an ordinary PNG or MKV, and every extraction is checked with a CRC-32.

## Highlights

- **Five embedding modes, each with a different trade-off**

  | Mode | Best for | Capacity at 1080p |
  |---|---|---|
  | `lsb` | invisible hiding in a lossless file | 759 KiB per bit depth |
  | `raw` | maximum capacity (the image turns to noise) | up to 6.2 MB |
  | `binary` | a sturdy, visible black-and-white pattern | 253 KiB |
  | `qim` | surviving a high-quality JPEG re-save | 253 KiB |
  | `dct` | surviving JPEG, H.264, VP9 and resizing | 3.4 KiB per frame |

- **Survives lossy processing.** A `dct` payload comes back intact after JPEG quality 75, H.264 up to CRF 28, VP9 up to CRF 40, a 30 → 24 fps conversion and a downscale-and-back, thanks to Reed–Solomon error correction.
- **Works on video.** The commands are the same as for images. Payloads can span frames, audio is preserved, and `--repeat` spreads copies across frames so a dropped frame costs one vote instead of the whole payload.
- **Self-describing.** `extract` detects the mode and its strength setting from the embedded header, so you never need to remember how a file was made.
- **Measured, not claimed.** `datum analyze` runs chi-square and RS steganalysis against a carrier. The robustness tables come from the included `datum_robustness` harness.

## Download

| Platform | File |
|---|---|
| Windows x86-64 | `datum-0.1.0-windows-x86_64.zip` |
| Linux x86-64 | `datum-0.1.0-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` |

Both binaries are statically linked and need no extra libraries. Each archive contains `datum` (`datum.exe` on Windows), `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` and `LICENSE`. On other platforms, [build from source](https://github.com/iEmreM/datum#getting-started) with a C++20 compiler and CMake 3.20 or newer.

**Video support needs [`ffmpeg`](https://ffmpeg.org/download.html) and `ffprobe` on your `PATH`.** They are not bundled. Images work without them.

To verify a download, compare it against `SHA256SUMS.txt`:

```sh
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt --ignore-missing          # Linux
Get-FileHash datum-0.1.0-windows-x86_64.zip           # Windows PowerShell
```

The Windows executable is not code-signed, so SmartScreen may warn the first time you run it.

## Quick start

```sh
datum --version
datum capacity -i photo.png --mode lsb
datum embed    -i photo.png -o stego.png -d secret.zip --mode lsb
datum extract  -i stego.png -o recovered.zip
```

The [README](https://github.com/iEmreM/datum#readme) walks through every mode, video and steganalysis step by step.

## Before you use it

- **`datum` is not encryption.** There is no key in this release, so anyone with `datum` can extract a payload. Encrypt files first (for example with `age`, `gpg` or an encrypted archive), then hide them.
- **The carrier format may change before 1.0.** The next planned release adds keyed embedding (`--key`), which may change the DTM1 header. The changelog will say whether carriers made with 0.1.0 can still be read.
- `dct` carriers must reach the decoder at their original size. Crops and size changes are not supported.
- None of the robustness figures have been measured against a real YouTube upload. They come from local ffmpeg encodes chosen to approximate one.
